analysis.title: CIO View: Treasury Inflation-Protected Securities
key_insights: Lower energy prices drove inflation expectations down over the last month and TIPS underperformed nominal Treasuries.
TIPS valuations look appealing: real yields are near 20-year highs and breakeven inflation rates are back at pre-war levels.

The 10-year breakeven fell 14bps to 2.21%, below its level at the outset of the Iran conflict. The 10-year TIPS real yield is 2.89% as of 18 November, against an early-October peak of 2.95%, the highest in almost 20 years.

TIPS perform best when real yields fall and inflation expectations rise. They tend to do well in supply-side oil shocks, which create a stagflationary environment, except when the central bank responds aggressively, as in 2022-23.
The rise in real yields reflects higher hawkish Fed expectations and better-than-expected economic activity. UBS thinks it will be hard for real yields to sustain a move above 3%.

Market pricing of 75bps of additional Fed tightening goes beyond UBS's expectation of 'recalibration hikes'. UBS sees signs it is tightening financial conditions in riskier assets, which should eventually moderate growth expectations and support TIPS through lower real yields.
Benchmark crude is down close to 20% since end-October, which drove the fall in inflation expectations and outweighed the upside surprise in October CPI.
Medium- to long-term breakevens cluster around 2.2% across the curve. The market is pricing disinflation from October CPI of 3.6% y/y, while core inflation is 2.6% y/y.
TIPS beat nominal Treasuries over their holding period only if CPI averages above the market-implied expectation. Persistence of inflation and pass-through from energy prices are the key variables.

Lower liquidity is a headwind for TIPS relative to nominals, especially in market stress. The inflation risk premium should support TIPS over a strategic horizon given geopolitics, fiscal dominance concerns and inflation above 2% for more than five years.
UBS Global Asset Class Preference for TIPS is Neutral.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Down 14bps over the last month to below the pre-Iran-conflict level, reflecting lower energy prices.
Close to the early-October peak of 2.95%, the highest in almost 20 years. UBS expects it to struggle to hold above 3%.
Upside surprise versus expectations, but breakevens near 2.2% imply the market expects disinflation.
May be a better signal of underlying inflation once the energy spike passes.
Market pricing exceeds UBS's expectation of 'recalibration hikes' and is starting to tighten financial conditions in riskier assets.
Main driver of the fall in inflation expectations.

risk_factors: A growth scare or market stress that weakens the economy so inflation falls faster than UBS anticipates and risk premiums widen would weaken TIPS relative to nominals.
A material growth slowdown or a sharp tightening in financial conditions would lower inflation expectations and favor nominal government bonds.
Lower TIPS liquidity relative to nominals, particularly in market stress.
An aggressive monetary policy response, as in 2022-23, hurts TIPS even in an oil shock.
Real yields rising above 3% would hurt TIPS returns.
geopolitical: Iran conflict: the 10-year breakeven is now below its level at the outset of the conflict.
Complex geopolitical environment cited as supporting the inflation risk premium.
Supply-side-driven oil shocks create a stagflationary environment.

tension_points.bull_case: Real yields near 20-year highs and breakevens at pre-war levels give an attractive setup. Real yields are likely to fall as tightening feeds into financial conditions, and persistent inflation or energy pass-through would favor TIPS over nominals.
tension_points.bear_case: A growth scare, market stress or sharp tightening in financial conditions would push inflation expectations lower, widen risk premiums and favor nominal bonds. Lower TIPS liquidity is also a headwind.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A growth scare or period of market stress that weakens the economy so inflation falls faster than UBS anticipates and risk premiums widen.

theme_stances.key_argument: Real yields near 20-year highs and breakevens back at pre-war levels make forward-looking TIPS returns attractive.
theme_stances.evidence: this mix of historically high real yields and cyclically low compensation
